channel.title: Pratik Dhanave — Blog
channel.description: Long-form writing on multi-agent AI, medical AI governance, HIPAA-aware architecture, and cloud-native systems.

item.title: Shipping MCP Securely to Production
item.description: An MCP server can run code and see context on the model's behalf. Authentication, prompt-injection and tool-poisoning risks, human-in-the-loop, sandboxing, and a production checklist.

item.title: Building a Self-Evolving Agent
item.description: Memory, grounded self-refinement, a verified skill library, and an evaluation gate combine into one buildable architecture that gets better as it runs — safely.

item.title: Building an MCP Client
item.description: Build an MCP client that launches a server, discovers its tools, and drives them from a language model — the core of what every MCP host does internally.

item.title: Evaluating Evolution — and Keeping It Safe
item.description: A system that changes itself can improve right off a cliff. Measuring evolution honestly, reward hacking, drift and collapse, and the guardrails that keep it safe.

item.title: Building an MCP Server from Scratch
item.description: Build a complete MCP server in Python with the official SDK — a notes service with a tool, a resource, and a prompt — and test it end to end with the MCP Inspector.

item.title: Population Methods and Automated Design
item.description: The most ambitious self-evolution searches a population of agent designs. Automated Design of Agentic Systems, evolutionary prompt search, debate, and self-play.

item.title: MCP Resources and Prompts
item.description: Beyond tools, MCP servers expose resources (read-only context by URI) and prompts (reusable templates). What each is for, how they appear on the wire, and how to choose.

item.title: Self-Critique and Its Limits
item.description: Self-critique is tempting but dangerous: without a real external signal, models often fail to self-correct and can get worse. Where self-critique works and where it drifts.

item.title: MCP Tools: Giving Agents the Power to Act
item.description: Tools are the MCP primitive that lets a model act. How to define them, the tools/list and tools/call methods, results versus errors, and designing tools a model can actually use.

item.title: Acquiring Tools and Skills
item.description: An agent that writes and banks its own verified skills grows more capable the longer it runs. Voyager's skill library and how to build a self-extending action space.

item.title: Claude Code in Production Workflows
item.description: The capstone: running Claude Code headless in scripts and CI (PR review, batch ops, scheduled jobs) — and the guardrails it demands: least privilege, sandboxing, gating the produced artifact with human review, and the series' layered recap.

item.title: Thriving as a Forward Deployed Engineer
item.description: The capstone: building a durable FDE career — the rewards and the hazards (context-switching, emotional labor, the maintenance trap), managing your capacity and boundaries, and growing toward staff engineering, product, leadership, or founding.

item.title: Building an AI Red-Team Program
item.description: The capstone: making red-teaming a sustained program — the remediation loop where findings become regression tests, blending automated/manual/external modes, rules of engagement, ship-blocking severity thresholds, governance evidence, and culture.

item.title: The Architect's Soft Skills and Leadership
item.description: The capstone: the non-technical skills that make or break an architect — communication tailored to the audience, influence without authority, leading technically while staying hands-on, mentoring, and avoiding the ivory tower.

item.title: AI-Assisted Code Review
item.description: The capstone: using AI/LLM reviewers well and where humans stay essential — AI as a tireless first pass that clears the noise, its limits (design judgment, contextual security, accountability, hallucinations), and a healthy human+AI division of labor.

item.title: Continuous Security: Monitoring, Compliance, and Culture
item.description: The capstone: shifting right to continuous security — runtime detection and vulnerability management as a loop, security observability and tamper-evident audit, compliance-as-code with evidence from the pipeline, metrics that matter, and the culture (paved roads, champions).

item.title: The Secure API Lifecycle
item.description: The capstone: baking security into the API lifecycle — shift-left threat modeling, CI gates (SAST, SCA, secret scanning, spec-driven authz/BOLA and DAST tests that fail the build), an OWASP-API-Top-10-to-control map, and incident response.

item.title: API Lifecycle and Governance
item.description: The capstone: designing and shipping consistent APIs at scale — the lifecycle, design review and style guides, linting the spec as policy-as-code in CI, contract testing so changes don't break consumers, an API catalog with ownership, and production observability.

item.title: Designing a System End to End
item.description: The capstone: one worked design end to end — requirements, estimation, API and data model, high-level architecture, and deep dives applying the whole series (scaling, caching, sharding, consistency, async, reliability) with explicit trade-offs.

item.title: AI Red-Teaming and Testing
item.description: Find AI security failures before attackers do: adversarial testing of the whole system, a test taxonomy mapped to the series, automated tooling (PyRIT, garak), a CI security-regression suite that fails the build, honest attack-success-rate measurement, and AI incident response.

item.title: MCP Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP
item.description: The same MCP messages travel over a subprocess pipe or the network — stdio for local tools, streamable HTTP for remote services. How each works and when to choose it.

item.title: Self-Refining Prompts and Instructions
item.description: The prompt is the agent's program. Self-Refine, DSPy, and Promptbreeder turn prompt engineering into an automated search the system runs on itself.

item.title: Skills and Slash Commands
item.description: Packaging repeatable workflows: custom slash commands for frequent explicit tasks, and skills — self-contained procedures the agent loads when relevant — turning tribal knowledge into invokable, versioned team assets. Matching the mechanism to frequency.

item.title: The FDE Toolkit and Technical Breadth
item.description: The FDE's edge is breadth, not deep single-stack mastery: comb-shaped competence across data, backend, a little frontend, and just-enough ops; choosing tools for speed and fit; a pragmatic default kit; and the meta-skills (learning speed, finishing) that outlast any framework.

item.title: Measuring and Scoring Red-Team Results
item.description: Turning attacks into metrics: attack success rate and why it's subtle, scoring success (rule/classifier/LLM-judge with its biases), coverage across the taxonomy, severity weighting, tracking trends per model/prompt version, and honest reporting of residual risk.

item.title: Evolutionary Architecture and Technical Debt
item.description: Architecture is never done: evolutionary architecture and fitness functions that guard characteristics in CI, technical debt done right (deliberate vs reckless, managing the interest), and incremental strangler-fig migration instead of the doomed big rewrite.

item.title: Code Review at Scale
item.description: Making review work across a team without becoming a bottleneck: review velocity as a first-class metric, ownership and routing (CODEOWNERS), automating toil so humans do judgment, healthy SLAs, and measuring the right things.

item.title: Container and Kubernetes Security
item.description: Securing the runtime platform: minimal non-root images scanned for CVEs, the container isolation model and hardening (drop caps, read-only FS, seccomp), and Kubernetes — Pod Security Standards, RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicies, and admission control (Gatekeeper/Kyverno).

item.title: API Gateways and Runtime Protection
item.description: The perimeter and runtime layer: the API gateway as a policy enforcement point (and why it can't replace per-service authz), WAF limits, improper inventory management (shadow/zombie APIs), security misconfiguration, and runtime detection.

item.title: Documentation and Developer Experience
item.description: An API is only as good as a developer's ability to succeed with it: OpenAPI as the machine-readable contract (docs, SDKs, mocks, contract tests), reference plus guides, errors as documentation, and optimizing time-to-first-successful-call.

item.title: Reliability and Resilience
item.description: Designing systems that survive failure: the nines and SLI/SLO/error budgets, eliminating single points of failure, timeouts and retries with backoff+jitter made safe by idempotency, circuit breakers, rate limiting and load shedding, and graceful degradation.

item.title: Building an AI Governance Program
item.description: The capstone: assemble a right-sized governance program — roles and accountability, a model/use-case inventory as the backbone, lifecycle gates, and policy-as-code that blocks deploy when an owner, risk tier, model card, eval pass, or monitor is missing.

item.title: Securing the AI Pipeline
item.description: DevSecOps for AI: secrets in a manager not code, least-privilege runtime identities (no ambient prod creds for agents), egress control, rate/spend limits against model DoS, supply-chain verification in CI, prompts-as-code, and a security-eval gate that fails the build.

item.title: Production on watsonx
item.description: Run a watsonx system in production from Python: IBM Cloud vs Cloud Pak for Data, project_id vs deployment spaces, reliability (tenacity retries, IAM token refresh, fallback), token-based cost, observability wired to watsonx.governance monitors, and securing IAM credentials.

item.title: Production on the NVIDIA Stack
item.description: Run an NVIDIA-stack LLM system in production from Python: hosted vs self-hosted vs hybrid, reliability (client retries, tenacity backoff, readiness probes, fallback), the GPU-hours cost model, Prometheus observability across the pipeline, and securing nvapi-/NGC keys.

item.title: The MCP Wire Protocol: JSON-RPC and the Connection Lifecycle
item.description: Under every MCP tool call is a JSON-RPC conversation that starts with an initialize handshake and a capability negotiation. Here is the wire protocol in detail.

item.title: Learning from Experience: Memory and Reflection
item.description: The cheapest way to make an agent evolve is to let it remember and reflect. Reflexion's verbal learning and the Generative Agents memory stream — and how to build a modest version.

item.title: Hooks and Automation
item.description: Hooks are shell commands that fire deterministically on lifecycle events — auto-format on edit, block edits to protected paths, run checks, notify. When to use a hook (guarantee) vs CLAUDE.md (influence) vs permissions (gate), and keeping them safe.

item.title: From Bespoke to Product
item.description: Every FDE builds one-offs; the ones who last turn them into product. Why bespoke is the right start, the 'third time productize' rule, the feedback loop to the product team, designing custom work for graduation, and managing the portfolio of one-offs.

item.title: Automated Red-Teaming and Tooling
item.description: Scaling red-teaming: the harness building blocks (attack seeds, mutation, orchestrator, scorer), adaptive LLM-driven attackers, the real tools by role (PyRIT, garak, promptfoo, Giskard), and integrating an automated red-team gate into CI.

item.title: Documenting Architecture
item.description: Communicating architecture so it survives contact with a team: the C4 model's zoomable levels, diagrams-as-code that live in version control and don't rot, multiple views for multiple audiences, and just-enough living docs plus ADRs.

item.title: Security and Performance Review
item.description: The specialist lenses: security review (untrusted input to a sink, missing authz/BOLA, secrets, SSRF, new dependencies) and performance review (N+1 queries, unbounded queries, missing indexes) — flag the smells, defer depth to scanners and profilers.

item.title: Infrastructure as Code Security and Policy as Code
item.description: Securing infrastructure definitions and enforcing guardrails automatically: IaC scanning (Checkov/tfsec/Trivy) for misconfig, drift detection, and policy-as-code with OPA/Rego + Conftest so org rules block bad infra before apply — not in a wiki.

item.title: Transport and Data Security
item.description: Protecting data in transit and at rest: TLS everywhere (even internal, zero-trust), mTLS for service-to-service, minimizing sensitive data exposure, encryption at rest with managed keys, secrets management, a correct CORS allow-list, and redacting logs.

item.title: Beyond REST: GraphQL and gRPC
item.description: When REST isn't the right shape: GraphQL (client-selected fields, and its N+1 / caching / complexity costs) and gRPC (Protobuf, HTTP/2, streaming, codegen) — plus a decision framework for REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC.

item.title: Asynchronous Processing and Messaging
item.description: Decoupling with queues and events: message queues vs pub/sub vs log-based streaming, delivery semantics (why exactly-once delivery is a myth — do idempotent processing), ordering, backpressure, the transactional outbox, and dead-letter queues.

item.title: The AI Regulatory Landscape
item.description: Orient in AI regulation and translate it into controls (not legal advice): the EU AI Act's risk tiers and obligations, ISO/IEC 42001 as a certifiable AI management system, NIST AI RMF, and a crosswalk mapping each obligation to the artifact that satisfies it.

item.title: Guardrails and Content Safety
item.description: The defensive layer that screens inputs and outputs: input/output/topical/groundedness rails, the real ecosystem (Llama Guard, Granite Guardian, NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Presidio, hosted moderation), and a vendor-neutral guardrail pipeline — with honest false-positive/negative trade-offs.

item.title: Governance and Monitoring with watsonx.governance
item.description: Governance is why many enterprises pick watsonx: model inventory, automated factsheets, monitoring (quality, drift, bias, and generative metrics like faithfulness), explainability, and EU AI Act-aligned risk workflows — with the ibm-watsonx-gov evaluation SDK and what to log.

item.title: Self-Hosting and Optimizing Inference
item.description: Move from the hosted API Catalog to self-hosted inference: run a NIM container (your Python client works unchanged by swapping base_url), use Triton directly via tritonclient, and understand the TensorRT-LLM levers — quantization, in-flight batching, paged KV cache, tensor parallelism.
